notes: `held` is what the party has about themselves. Nothing in it has been disclosed by the act of holding it — story 11 step 2 is explicit, and the two lists are separate here for that reason
`sent` is per counterparty and carries `at`, so 'what I told whom, and when' is answerable after the fact (step 6). `pending: true` is disclosure chosen at formation on a tally not yet countersigned

`received` is what the counterparty says about themselves. It is their claim, not something Taleus verified (path E), and a key absent from it is absent — the fixture cannot say whether it was withheld or never held, because neither can the app
`requests` runs both ways: `from: them` is path B, an ask that turns silence into a yes or no; `from: me` is path E step 4. An answer of `refused` carries no value and is not a failure
`held` deliberately has no `taxId`: Northwind's standing request is path A, something the party is not willing to give, and refusing must be a first-class answer
`reachable: false` in the `error` variant is the story's error case — a correction that cannot be delivered right now. It is per counterparty, because only some of a set will fail
